headline: House Prosecutors Weigh Asking Impeachment Court to Treat Michael Poa as Hostile Witness
seoTitle: Prosecutors Eye Michael Poa as Hostile Witness | FMB News
seoDescription: House prosecutors are preparing to seek hostile-witness treatment for OVP counsel Michael Poa as the Senate impeachment trial moves toward its next round of testimony.
deck: The prosecution says it is preparing a motion that would allow leading questions when the former DepEd undersecretary and current OVP counsel takes the stand.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: House prosecution managers said they are preparing to ask the Senate Impeachment Court to treat former Department of Education undersecretary and current Office of the Vice President counsel Michael Poa as a hostile or adverse witness when he testifies.

Lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro said the planned request is tied to Poa's current role with the Vice President's legal team and his previous responsibilities during the period being examined in the impeachment proceedings.

sections.heading: What prosecutors want to examine
paragraphs: According to the approved FMB News overnight brief, questioning is expected to focus on administrative explanations and formal replies sent to the Commission on Audit concerning confidential-fund liquidation during 2022 and 2023.

A hostile-witness designation, if granted by the presiding officer, would affect how prosecutors may question Poa, including the use of leading questions. The request itself would not establish the truth of any allegation under examination.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The impeachment court has also tightened rules governing out-of-court publicity while allowing both sides to present evidence and examine witnesses in the Senate plenary. Separately, financial institutions are working toward a September 2 deadline for subpoenaed records identified by the court.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The designation could shape the prosecution's examination of a witness who has both prior executive experience in the agencies under scrutiny and a current legal role connected to the Vice President. The Senate Impeachment Court, however, remains responsible for ruling on the request and weighing the evidence presented by both sides.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next key development is whether prosecutors formally move for hostile-witness treatment and how the defense and presiding officer respond when Poa is called. Any testimony should be assessed as evidence presented in an ongoing trial, not as a final finding of liability.
